questions.title: Probability 01
questions.prompt: 1. What is the probability of getting tails when flipping an unbiased coin?
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 02
questions.prompt: 2. What is the probability of drawing an Ace from a standard deck of cards?
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 03
questions.prompt: 3. What is the probability of rolling a 5 with a standard, unbiased, six-sided die?
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 04
questions.prompt: 4. What is the probability of getting two threes from rolling two standard, unbiased, six-sided die?
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 05
questions.prompt: 5. Determine the odds of drawing a number card with value 5 or lower from a standard deck of cards.
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%). For “odds”, a probability is accepted; for a 52-card deck, number cards are 2–10.

questions.title: Probability 06
questions.prompt: 6. What is the probability of flipping heads on two coin tosses? How about one head and one tail?
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 07
questions.prompt: 7. Determine the odds of flipping 5 straight heads in 5 coin flips.
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 08
questions.prompt: 8. Determine the probability of drawing a red, face card from a standard deck of cards.
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 09
questions.prompt: 9. What is the probability of rolling a prime number from a standard, unbiased, six-sided die?
questions.notes: Use a fraction (e.g. 1/2), decimal (0.5) or percentage (50%).

questions.title: Probability 10 · Bonus
questions.prompt: 10. What is the probability of drawing a Royal Flush from a standard deck of cards?
questions.notes: Assume a 5-card poker hand drawn uniformly from 52 cards.

questions.title: Calculate client age
questions.prompt: Q #1: Determine the age of each client above.
questions.notes: Example: Alex Arin, birthdate 1985-01-01; calculate completed years as of 2026-11-19. The source exercise requests an age for each client; the online checker samples one row.

questions.title: Total deposits
questions.prompt: Q #2: How much is the total Deposit?
questions.notes: Use all Deposit rows regardless of status, as the question does not add a status filter.

questions.title: Extract payment reference ID
questions.prompt: Q #3: Determine the PRID by getting the last 2 digits of the Transaction ID
questions.notes: For the first synthetic row, Transaction_ID = 7300000001. Enter the final two digits, or a RIGHT(J2,2) formula.

questions.title: Count centenarians
questions.prompt: Q #4: How many clients are centenarians?

questions.title: Average deposit size
questions.prompt: Q #5: What is the average Deposit size?

questions.title: Successful withdrawal amount
questions.prompt: Q #6: How much Withdrawal has approved and has gone Successful?
questions.notes: Here “approved” is interpreted as Status=Successful, because the source table has no separate approval field.

questions.title: Concatenate full address
questions.prompt: Q #7: Populate the Full Address Column in the format "Address 1, Address 2"
questions.notes: First sample row: Address_1=Dubai; Address_2=UAE. Enter the combined address or an Excel formula.

questions.title: Pivot: transaction × payment method
questions.prompt: Q #8: Create a Pivot Table showing the amounts per Transaction and per Payment Method.
questions.notes: A full Excel PivotTable is a grid; the online checker tests three cells from that pivot. Use SUM of Amount; blank intersections are zero.

questions.title: Count transactions below 1,000,000
questions.prompt: Q #9: How many transactions of less than 1,000,000 were made?

questions.title: Extract first and last names
questions.prompt: Q #10: Create two columns at the end of the table detailing the customer's First Name and Last Name.
questions.notes: Use the first fictional client: Alex Arin. Enter the values or Excel formulas.

questions.title: Filter Bank payments
questions.prompt: 1. Create a SELECT query that will give you all 'Bank' transactions as indicated in the Payment_Method column.
questions.notes: Write a SQLite query using table transactions_hst.

questions.title: Aggregate by transaction type
questions.prompt: 2. Create a SELECT query that will give you a summary of how much transaction we took in per Transaction_Type.
questions.notes: Write a SQLite query using table transactions_hst.

questions.title: Successful volume by payment method
questions.prompt: 3. Create a SELECT query that will give you a summary of how much 'Successful' transaction we took in per Payment_Method.
questions.notes: Write a SQLite query using table transactions_hst.

questions.title: Delete declined rows (sandbox)
questions.prompt: 4. Create a query that will delete all entries for transactions that have been 'Declined'.
questions.notes: The query runs in an isolated, disposable, in-browser SQLite database. A DELETE never changes saved datasets.

questions.prompt: Calculate decline rate by payment method (additional portfolio exercise).
questions.notes: Write a SQLite query using table transactions_hst.

questions.title: Rank customers by transaction volume
questions.prompt: Rank customers by total transaction amount using a CTE and a window function (additional exercise).
questions.notes: Write a SQLite query using table transactions_hst.

questions.prompt: Find duplicate Transaction_ID values (additional data-quality exercise).
